name: בִּנְיָמִין
summary: Jacob’s youngest son, Rachel’s second, and the tribe that came from him (Num 10:24); also a man of Bilhan’s house in Benjamin’s own line (1Ch 7:10) and men of the return in Ezra and Nehemiah. Rachel, dying in childbirth, named him בֶּן־אוֹנִי, “son of my sorrow”, and his father renamed him בִּנְיָמִין: the first word, בֵּן “son”, stays, and the second becomes יָמִין, the right hand, the hand of favour and strength (Gen 35:18; 48:14). The text itself divides the name so: a Benjamite is בֶּן־יְמִינִי (1Sa 9:21; Jdg 3:15), and Psalm 80, which names Benjamin, prays for “the man of your right hand, the son of man” (Psa 80:3, 18).

evidence.note: She called his name בֶּן־אוֹנִי, and his father called him בִנְיָמִין: “son” kept, “my sorrow” changed to “right hand”.
Saul: “Am I not בֶן־יְמִינִי, of the smallest of the tribes of Israel … of the tribe of בִנְיָמִן?”: the name as בֶּן + יְמִינִי.
Ehud בֶּן־הַיְמִינִי, a Benjamite, “a man bound in his right hand” (אִטֵּר יַד־יְמִינוֹ).
Israel puts his right hand (יְמִינוֹ) on the younger, Ephraim: the right hand as the hand of the greater blessing.
Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh, stir up your might.
Let your hand be on אִישׁ יְמִינֶךָ, on בֶּן־אָדָם whom you made strong for yourself.
Over the host of the tribe of בְּנֵי בִנְיָמִן was Abidan the son of Gideoni.
Of Benjamin: the beloved of Yahweh shall dwell in safety by him.
Benjamin, of the sons of Harim, who had taken a foreign wife.
Benjamin and Hasshub repaired over against their house.
Benjamin, at the dedication of the wall.

note: The second element is יָמִין (root ימן), which has no entry of its own yet; this name is linked to the בֵּן entry by agreement with the ימן item, which will not write it. The verse evidence for “right hand” is cited here directly. יָמִין also means “south” (Psa 89:13), and a “son of the south” reading is possible (Benjamin alone was born in Canaan, his brothers in Paddan-aram to the north); Gen 35:18’s contrast with “son of my sorrow” and Gen 48:14 favour “right hand”. b.ca.ar (בֶּן־יְמִינִי, gentilic) is claimed here; it is double-filed on some plain יְמִינִי “my right hand” tokens (Psa 73:23; 137:5; Jer 22:24). The short gentilic יְמִינִי (j.bs.ad, j.bs.ah) is left to the ימן item. Ben-oni (b.ca.ad), Rachel’s name for him, has no entry. The Benjamin Gate (Jer 20:2; Zec 14:10) is a place and not tagged.
